derivation: from an unused root meaning to curb;
def: a halter (as restraining); by implication, the jaw

words.word: and there shall be a bridle

occurrences.text: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.
Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding: whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle, lest they come near unto thee.

And his breath, as an overflowing stream, shall reach to the midst of the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of vanity: and there shall be a bridle in the jaws of the people, causing them to err.
